area: TS architecture: the ECS claim + type hardening

item_verdicts.title: Adopt ECS (bitECS or custom) for the Sim
item_verdicts.why: Both kills verified against the repo. (1) tests/config-purity.test.ts checkImports() (line 37) asserts every src/core import resolves inside core/ or config/ with the exact message "bare import ... core/ is framework-free" — a bitECS import literally cannot pass. (2) Scale claim holds: SimSetup is 1 player + N enemies, PROJECTILE_MAX_ACTIVE=8 (config/combat-sim.ts) caps kunai arena-wide, and the determinism doc is quoted accurately (Sim.ts lines 69-70: "Spawn order is identity AND iteration order... what keeps a crowd deterministic"). 894 tests measured green by running npm test (56 files). Source spot-checks pass: HN 27754996 really contains "Hardly any game needs 'thousands of interacting entities'" plus the profile-first consensus, and simplified.media/guides/ecs-browser-games is live and itself says ECS pays off "once entity counts climb into the thousands" while small fixed rosters don't need it. One trivial slip, not verdict-changing: the 8-mob figure sits in the ledger's adjacent "simultaneous attackers" row ("With 8 on screen the player's hit rate is no higher than 1v1"), not the "waves spawn by falling in from above" row; neither row is touched by the §00b or §S24-H corrections.

item_verdicts.title: Branded unit types for the three pixel systems (px@1080 / stage px / world px)
item_verdicts.why: Every factual anchor checks out. Sim.ts PlayerIntent.moveTargetX is doc-commented "mouse hold-to-run target X (stage px)" (line 140-141) while DuelScene.ts stores mouseTargetX WORLD-side (header comment lines 89-90: "dragPoints and mouseTargetX are stored WORLD-side"; stageToWorld applied at the pointer handlers, lines 258-269) — the Sim-side comment does lie across the seam exactly as claimed, and the dead_ends section honestly downgraded this from live bug to bug-class. config/display.ts confirms GAME_WIDTH=1024, WORLD_WIDTH=800 (ratio 1.28) and carries the WORLD-vs-STAGE prose block the implementation note targets. Ledger line 9 reads verbatim "Conversion: px @1080 ÷ 1.875 = stage px (canvas 1024×576)" and is not corrected by §00b/§S24-H. Goldberg's article (fetched) shows the intersection-brand pattern and the exact caveat cited: binary operations on branded numeric types raise no type errors (TS#59423), which supports boundaries-only ADAPT over whole-Sim branding. A type-only brand in src/config is compatible with config/CLAUDE.md's no-logic rule.

item_verdicts.title: Branded/template-literal tagging for CONTRACT vs INFERRED config values
item_verdicts.why: The claimed enforcement gap is real: src/config/CLAUDE.md states "Every value is labeled CONTRACT / INFERRED / Spec-fixed" under a header claiming test enforcement, but grepping both tests/config-purity.test.ts and tests/config-values.test.ts finds no check that config exports carry an evidence label (the only 'label' hits are checkImports' parameter name; config-values pins numeric values, not doc comments). The repo idiom cited exists exactly as described: config-purity.test.ts self-tests the scanner against fixtures (describe 'scanner self-test', tests/fixtures/scan-probe), tests/utils/configPurity.ts exports LiteralHit, and CONTRACT-SRC really appears in src/config/combat.ts (three hits), so the proposed label set is correct to include it. Routing to a scanner gate rather than a strippable type brand matches the standing build-the-tooling rule and the double-entry ratchet documented in src/config/CLAUDE.md. The negative research claim (no practitioner precedent for provenance-tagging constants via types) is consistent with the honest dead_ends admission.

item_verdicts.title: Exhaustiveness checking via `satisfies never` on the SimEvent drain
item_verdicts.why: The core survives every check: SimEvent is a discriminated union in Sim.ts drained by DuelScene.ts via a plain if/else-if chain on ev.type (lines 507-542) with guarded cases exactly as described (ev.type === 'damage' && ev.target === 'player', line 524), so an unhandled new variant is silently dropped today; EncounterScene.ts line 136 is a second drain site (the 'grep for drainEvents callers' note is right); eslint.config.mjs exists at repo root; the typescript-eslint rule page is real and does reference a satisfies-never default. But two stated facts are wrong: (1) SimEvent has 17 variants (Sim.ts lines 112-130), not 18; (2) the typescript-eslint docs do not 'explicitly endorse the satisfies never default' as a general recommendation — it appears only in a caveat about disabling allowDefaultCaseForExhaustiveSwitch, offered as an alternative (paired with the eslint core default-case rule) for projects with many intentionally redundant default cases.
item_verdicts.correction: SimEvent is a 17-variant union (count Sim.ts lines 112-130: fightStarted through autoStroke), not 18. And cite the typescript-eslint source precisely: the rule's docs mention `satisfies never` in a caveat as an alternative pattern (disable allowDefaultCaseForExhaustiveSwitch + eslint core default-case rule + `satisfies never` in kept defaults), not as a blanket endorsement. Neither error changes the ADOPT verdict — the unguarded if/else drain and the zero-runtime-cost fix are real.

item_verdicts.title: Template-literal types for actor/entity identity
item_verdicts.why: ALREADY_DONE is exactly right, verified line-by-line in src/core/Sim.ts: `export type ActorId = 'player' | \`enemy${number}\`` (line 72, doc comment attributes it to SESSION14 A1 / §3.5 A), PLAYER_ID exported as the one fixed name (line 75), enemyIdAt(i) as the private constructor (line 78), and Sim.actor() throws `Sim: unknown actor id` on lookup misses (lines 377-383) with a doc comment giving precisely the rationale claimed (a typo'd id silently resolving would be an invisible damage bug). The id surface is both statically shaped and runtime-guarded; nothing to add.

overall_note: The research output survives adversarial verification almost intact: 4 of 5 items CONFIRMED, 1 WEAKENED on two citation-precision errors (SimEvent is 17 variants not 18; typescript-eslint's satisfies-never mention is a caveat-section alternative, not an explicit endorsement) that do not change its ADOPT adjudication. Source spot-checks (4 URLs fetched, including both C-grade ones I suspected fabricated) all came back live and supportive — notably the HN quote is near-verbatim and Goldberg's arithmetic-stripping caveat is real (TS#59423). Repo checks all passed against the actual files: the core/ bare-import ban, the moveTargetX stage-px/world-px comment lie, the missing label-coverage gate, the if/else event drain, and the shipped ActorId template-literal type. Ledger checks passed: the ÷1.875 conversion row and the 8-mob row exist and neither is overturned by §00b or §S24-H (one trivial slip: the 8-on-screen figure is in the adjacent 'simultaneous attackers' row, not the 'waves spawn by falling in from above' row). Test count independently measured: 894 passing across 56 files. Adjudication logic (REJECT ECS, ADAPT-at-boundaries branding, scanner-not-types for labels, ADOPT satisfies-never, ALREADY_DONE ids) is sound against the repo's invariants and the fidelity prime directive.
